mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about liquids is a common misconception?

options.B: Liquids take the shape of their container.

mcqs.explanation: Liquids do not have a fixed shape; they adopt the shape of the container they are in. Option A states the opposite, making it the misconception. Options B and C correctly describe liquid properties, and D is true because liquids do have a fixed volume.

mcqs.learning_point: Taking the shape of a container
mcqs.question: Why does water poured into a glass assume the shape of the glass?

options.A: Because its particles are tightly packed and cannot move.
options.B: Because its particles are loosely packed and can move past each other, allowing the liquid to conform to the container.
options.C: Because liquids have strong attractive forces that keep them rigid.
options.D: Because liquids are compressible and expand to fill space.

mcqs.answer: Because its particles are loosely packed and can move past each other, allowing the liquid to conform to the container.
mcqs.explanation: In liquids, particles are close but not fixed; they can slide past one another. This mobility lets the liquid take the shape of any container. Option A describes solids, C incorrectly suggests rigidity, and D confuses compressibility (liquids are nearly incompressible).

mcqs.question: Which statement best compares the ability to flow of liquids and solids?

options.A: Both liquids and solids flow equally because their particles are equally free to move.
options.B: Liquids flow easily because their particles can slide past each other, whereas solids retain shape because their particles are locked in place.
options.C: Solids flow more easily than liquids because solids have weaker intermolecular forces.
options.D: Neither liquids nor solids can flow; only gases can.

mcqs.answer: Liquids flow easily because their particles can slide past each other, whereas solids retain shape because their particles are locked in place.
mcqs.explanation: Liquid particles are not fixed; they can move past one another, giving liquids the ability to flow. In solids, particles are arranged in a fixed lattice, so the shape remains constant. Options A and C are incorrect descriptions of particle behavior, and D ignores the flow property of liquids.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a liquid at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: At typical room temperature (around 20‑25 °C), water, mercury, and olive oil are all liquids. Ice is the solid form of water, so it is not a liquid. This tests knowledge of common liquid examples.
